title: wall-wol output
description: Sends Wake-on-LAN magic packets to wake devices. Usage: wall-wol MAC [MAC ...] [--broadcast IP] [--port 9] [--count 3] [--interval-ms 100]. Sending a packet does not prove the device woke up: Wake-on-LAN has no reply.

status.description: ok: finished with no errors. partial: finished, result present but incomplete (see errors). error: failed, result is null.

result.description: Tool-specific payload; null when status is error.

allOf.$comment: partial -> at least one error, result present
error -> at least one error, result is null

schema_version.description: Contract version, MAJOR.MINOR. This file is the contract for major version 1: every 1.x document must validate against it.

name.description: Program that produced the document, e.g. "wall-scan".

version.description: Package version of that program (its git tag without the leading v). Independent of schema_version.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC with a Z suffix, e.g. "2026-10-08T09:30:00Z". Fractional seconds allowed.

code.description: Machine-readable snake_case code. Open set: new codes may appear in any minor version, so consumers must handle codes they do not know.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show in the UI.

target.description: The input (usually an IP address) this error is about, or null for an error affecting the whole run.

params.description: The run-wide inputs. The MAC addresses are in result.targets.

broadcast.description: Destination IPv4 address of the packets: 255.255.255.255 (the default) or a private address, normally the broadcast address of the device's network, e.g. 192.168.1.255.

count.description: Magic packets sent to each MAC address.

interval_ms.description: Pause between rounds of packets, in milliseconds.

source_ip.description: The local IPv4 address the packets left from, chosen by the routing table for the destination. It shows which network they went out on: with several network cards, 255.255.255.255 leaves through the one with the default route, which may not be the device's network. null if the operating system does not say.

targets.description: One entry per MAC address, in the order given. A repeated address is listed, and sent packets, once.

packets_sent.description: Magic packets handed to the network for this address: params.count, unless sending failed part-way (status is then partial). Wake-on-LAN has no reply, so this does not prove the device woke up.
